title: MiniFleet v0.2: autonomy on failure, deployment, fleet metrics
summary: The fleet upgrades itself: it adopts its own codebase, adds the three capabilities it was missing (bounded self-repair from gate evidence, a supervised deploy-and-observe stage, and fleet-level metrics), and proves it did not break the existing engine.
intent: Continue replicating Fleet by making MiniFleet more autonomous. It must be able to (1) turn a failed task into a repair packet that a worker can act on, bounded by a maximum number of attempts, (2) actually deploy a produced system: start it, wait for its ready line, probe it, soak it for a short window and shut it down, and (3) account for its own runs - attempts, retries, gate outcomes and the critical path through the task graph. All three must be reachable from the CLI. The existing engine behaviour must be preserved: the current regression suite is the floor, not a suggestion.
deliverables: minifleet/repair.py - turn gate evidence into a bounded, actionable repair packet
minifleet/deploy.py - supervised process launch, ready detection, smoke and soak probes
minifleet/fleetmetrics.py - attempts, retries, gate outcomes and critical path of a run
cli wiring so `repair`, `deploy` and `fleetmetrics` are real subcommands
the existing engine tests, still green
constraints: the frozen contract in contracts/C-V02.md is not renegotiable
harness/ is frozen: workers may read it, never modify it
no new third-party dependency may be introduced
out_of_scope: publishing to a cloud provider; deploy means supervised local execution in the workspace

acceptance.statement: A repair packet lists only the failing gates, in gate-id order, carries the task write scope and never mutates its inputs
Repair is bounded: once the attempt budget is exhausted the packet sets escalate instead of proposing another attempt
A supervisor starts a process, parses its ready line and port, times out without hanging when no ready line arrives, and always tears the process down
Smoke and soak probes report status, sample count, failure count and latency percentiles
Fleet metrics report tasks, merged, failed, attempts, retries, gate outcomes and the critical path through the task graph
repair, deploy and fleetmetrics are CLI subcommands; repair writes one repair packet per failed task and reports cleanly when nothing failed
The pre-existing engine behaviour is unchanged: the regression suite that shipped with the baseline still passes on the integrated tree
The regression suite still finishes within 60 seconds

gates.title: worker's own tests plus the baseline suite
engine regression on the integrated tree

contracts.summary: Frozen interfaces for the three v0.2 modules and the CLI surface that exposes them.

exports.minifleet.repair.build_repair_packet: build_repair_packet(task: dict, evidence: list[dict], attempt: int, max_attempts: int = 3) -> dict with keys task_id, attempt, max_attempts, escalate, reason, failing_gates[{gate_id,status,detail}], instructions[list[str]], scope[list[str]], carry_forward[list[str]]
exports.minifleet.deploy.Supervisor: Supervisor(argv: list[str], cwd: str, ready_prefix: str = 'MINIFLEET_READY', timeout: float = 30.0) with .start() -> Supervisor, .wait_ready() -> {'ready': bool, 'port': int|None, 'seconds': float, 'stdout_tail': str}, .stop(timeout: float = 10.0) -> int, .running -> bool
exports.minifleet.deploy.smoke: smoke(url: str, timeout: float = 5.0) -> {'status': int, 'ok': bool, 'seconds': float}
exports.minifleet.deploy.soak: soak(url: str, seconds: float, interval: float = 0.25, timeout: float = 5.0) -> {'samples': int, 'failures': int, 'ok': bool, 'p50_ms': float, 'max_ms': float}
exports.minifleet.fleetmetrics.summarize: summarize(run: dict) -> {'tasks': int, 'merged': int, 'failed': int, 'attempts_total': int, 'retries': int, 'gates_total': int, 'gates_passed': int, 'gates_failed': int, 'critical_path_seconds': float, 'slowest_task': {'id': str, 'seconds': float} | None, 'verdict': str}
exports.minifleet cli: python3 -m minifleet repair --run DIR writes packets/<task>.repair.json for every failed task and prints 'no failed tasks' when there are none; python3 -m minifleet deploy --dir DIR --cmd CMD --probe PATH [--seconds N] starts the process, waits for its ready line, smokes and soaks the probe path, prints a JSON report and exits non-zero when the probe fails; python3 -m minifleet fleetmetrics --run DIR prints the summarize() JSON on stdout

contracts.content:
## Behavioural notes

### repair
`failing_gates` contains every evidence entry whose status is not `pass`, sorted by `gate_id`. `instructions` is a non-empty list of short, imperative sentences that name the failing gate ids so a worker can act without reading the ledger. `scope` is a copy of `task['owns']`. `carry_forward` is a copy of `task.get('submitted_files', [])`. `escalate` is True when `attempt >= max_attempts`. `reason` is a one-line summary of the failure. The function must not mutate `task` or `evidence`.

### deploy
`Supervisor.wait_ready()` reads the child's stdout line by line until a line starts with `ready_prefix`, parses the JSON payload after it (so `{"port": 4242}` yields `port=4242`), and returns within `timeout` seconds. On timeout it returns `ready: False` and a `stdout_tail` of what was seen; it must not hang and must leave `running` False after `stop()`. `stop()` sends SIGTERM, waits up to its timeout, escalates to SIGKILL if needed, and returns the exit code.
`smoke(url)` performs one GET and returns the status code, whether it was 2xx (`ok`), and the elapsed seconds. `soak(url, seconds, interval)` repeats GETs until `seconds` have elapsed, counts samples and failures (non-2xx counts as a failure), and reports `p50_ms`/`max_ms`. A dead endpoint must produce failures rather than an exception.

### fleetmetrics
`summarize(run)` takes a decoded `run.json`. `critical_path_seconds` is the longest chain of task durations following `depends_on` edges - it is not the sum of all durations. Task duration is `finished_at - started_at`, treated as 0 when either bound is missing. `slowest_task` is the task with the largest duration, or None when there are no tasks. `retries` is the sum of `max(attempts - 1, 0)`. `merged` counts tasks in state `merged`.

### CLI
`repair` must work on a run directory that contains only `run.json` plus a `packets/` directory, creating `packets/` if needed. It must not require a git repository.

components.name: Bounded self-repair
components.responsibility: Implement minifleet/repair.py, turning gate evidence into an actionable, bounded repair packet.
done_when: build_repair_packet matches the frozen signature and returns every documented key
failing gates are ordered by gate_id and exclude every passing gate
instructions name each failing gate id
the attempt budget is respected: escalate is set once it is exhausted
tests: unit tests covering ordering, escalation, empty evidence and non-mutation

components.name: Deploy and observe
components.responsibility: Implement minifleet/deploy.py: supervised process launch with ready detection, plus smoke and soak probes.
done_when: Supervisor.start/wait_ready/stop behave as specified and never leak a child process
a missing ready line returns ready False within the timeout instead of hanging
smoke reports status, ok and elapsed time
soak reports samples, failures, ok, p50_ms and max_ms, and survives a dead endpoint
tests: tests that spawn a real child process and a real in-process HTTP server

components.name: Fleet metrics
components.responsibility: Implement minifleet/fleetmetrics.py: account for a run - attempts, retries, gate outcomes and the critical path.
done_when: summarize returns every documented key for a realistic run record
the critical path follows depends_on edges and is not the sum of all durations
an empty run summarises without raising
tests: unit tests over synthetic run records, including a branching graph

components.name: CLI and scheduler wiring
components.responsibility: Wire the three new modules into the CLI (repair, deploy, fleetmetrics subcommands) and into the scheduler, without changing existing behaviour.
done_when: python3 -m minifleet --help lists repair, deploy and fleetmetrics
repair writes packets/<task>.repair.json for each failed task and prints 'no failed tasks' otherwise
deploy starts a command, waits for its ready line, probes it, prints JSON and always tears it down
every pre-existing subcommand and its behaviour is preserved
tests: a CLI-level test that drives the fixture run directory through the new subcommands
